newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Caraiba sees higher copper wire rod exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Caraiba sees higher copper wire rod exports.

text.p: Brazilian copper producer Caraiba Metais is expecting exports of copper wire rods to non-Mercosul countries to reach 4,800 tonnes in 1997 compared with practically nothing in 1996, a company official said.
"Last year we shipped a trial lot of 15 tonnes to Japan. This year we are expecting to ship 4,800 tonnes," said Hernani da Silveira, head of Caraiba's customer services division.

All of this year's sales are expected to go to South Korea. Caraiba in April started shipping 300 tonnes a month to Samsung under a one-year contract and is waiting to ship the first lot of a three-month contract to Daewoo.
The Daewoo contract is also for 300 tonnes a month but the first lot is for 360 tonnes at Daewoo's request.

The copper was due to have been loaded in the "Nedloyd Singapura" in the port of Salvador but the ship is currently docked in Santos and is not planning to come to Salvador until a labor dispute in Salvador port is resolved, da Silveira said.
Portworkers have been working to a go-slow since last week and loading rates have dropped to 25 containers per day from a usual 250 containers a day, he added.

Negotiations to resolve the dispute were being held today but if a solution is not found by the end of the week, Caraiba will have to transport the copper by land to Santos involving an estimated cost of 60 reais per tonne, da Silveira said.
This however will ensure the copper is delivered in time by the end of July, he added.
The port dispute has already resulted in Caraiba sending overland 100 tonnes of copper destined for Mercosur countries while a further 100 tonnes is expected to be transported the same way this week.
Caraiba normally sends 1,300-1,500 tonnes of copper wire rods to Mercosur destinations each month.
The go-slow is also preventing two ships which have just arrived from docking and loading a total of 5,000 tonnes of copper cathodes, destined for New Orleans in the U.S., da Silveira said.
Caraiba is Brazil's only copper producer and is part of metals mega-company Paranapanema formed last year.
Electrolytic copper production reached around 172,000 last year and is expected to increase to 190,000 tonnes in 1997.
Total exports last year were 53,905 tonnes of which 12,368 tonnes were of wire rods to Mercosur countries.
Sales of wire rods to the region are expected to rise to 16,000 tonnes in 1997, da Silveira said.
